title: CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check)
summary: CRC is an error-detecting code based on polynomial division. Data is treated as a polynomial; divided by a generator polynomial; remainder is the CRC. Common CRCs: CRC-8 (0x07), CRC-16-CCITT (0x1021), CRC-32 (0x04C11DB7, used in Ethernet, ZIP, PNG), CRC-64 (0x000000000000001B). Properties: detects all single-bit errors, all double-bit errors (for CRC width ≥ 2), all odd-bit errors (if generator has factor x+1), burst errors up to width bits.

structure.meaning: Process data byte by byte. For each byte, XOR with CRC register, look up in table, shift. O(n) with table, O(n*w) without.
Polynomial 0x04C11DB7. Used in Ethernet (FCS), ZIP, PNG, gzip, and many other formats.
Polynomial 0x1021. Used in X.25, HDLC, and many telecom protocols.
Polynomial 0x07. Used in SMBus, I2C, and small packets.
Detects: all single-bit errors, all double-bit errors (width ≥ 2), all odd-bit errors (if gen has x+1 factor), burst errors ≤ width bits.

notes: CRC is not a cryptographic hash (easily forged). Used for error detection, not security.
CRC-32 is the most common (Ethernet FCS, ZIP, PNG, gzip).
Table-driven CRC is O(n) with a 256-entry lookup table.
Bit-by-bit CRC is O(n*w) but needs no table.
CRCs are linear: CRC(a XOR b) = CRC(a) XOR CRC(b) (for same length). This property is used in attacks.
